lead: twenty minutes into meeting someone, off a pause and a name they went round, the account they lead with is open on the table — and they will not be in the room when you go further down.
sun: with people you have known for years there is at least something in the room that flinches. a stranger costs you nothing, so the descent runs at full speed from the handshake: under the job they gave you, under the reason they gave for leaving it, down to the thing that actually moved them, which is usually not creditable and is usually correct. you do not get this wrong at parties.
moon: the material comes in from across a room, and nothing in you releases it. the digging carries on after the person has gone home, on a face you saw once, on evidence they will never be asked about. what you arrive at cannot be put to them, and no second meeting is coming to correct it. the stranger stays, entire, at the depth you took them to.
pull: they went home whole, as far as they know. the true account of them stayed in the room, at the depth you took it to, held by somebody whose surname they never learned.
tension: people who have met you once describe you as intense, in the tone kept for somebody who asked one question too many. the small version of an introduction — what you do, where you grew up, how you know the host — has never worked in your hands, because the floor under it opens on the second answer. so you are known, widely and at distance, by people who cannot say what you do.
cost: everyone you meet is read to the bottom of themselves inside an evening, which is why nobody who lies for a living has ever got anywhere with you. what you never get is the ordinary long acquaintance where a person is allowed to be provisional. they are all settled already, sized in one evening, on grain nobody else picked up, by someone they would not recognise in the street.

lead: the founding story of the place is four generations old and you got under it in your second year in the chair. nobody stopped you, because nothing about the way you did it looked like damage.
sun: rank hands you the papers. the minute-books, the terms the place was set up on, the reason given for the arrangement everyone has worked under since — all of it is yours for the asking, and the asking is unremarkable coming from your seat. so the search reaches what no junior could have reached: the account of how this place became entitled to what it holds. the account did not hold.
moon: a level voice is what stops a room from calling something an attack. you asked for the papers the way you ask for anything, sat through what came out without your face moving, and the building read the whole operation as housekeeping. by the time anyone understood that the thing being examined was the ground the building stands on, it was already up and lying in the corridor.
pull: the question of whether you deserved a seat you did not build was never going to be left alone. it is settled now, in the sense that there is nothing left to deserve.
tension: a term is supposed to leave the place standing, and the word for someone whose term did not leave it standing is not a generous word. it will be used by people who are correct about the outcome and wrong about the sequence — they think you arrived intending this. you arrived wanting to know what you were sitting on, and the wanting has no off position, and finding out and taking it away are the same motion.
cost: an institution's founding fact only ever gets checked by somebody with the access and no instinct to look away, and you were the first of those to sit here. what the place can no longer do is tell anyone the story of itself. your successor inherits a seat, a term, and a record with nothing underneath it worth handing on.

lead: you are known for finding what a thing is standing on, and The Mane set the size of that reputation before you had any say in it, so the finding has an audience before it has a result.
sun: the work needs privacy it is never going to get. going under a thing means opening it before you know what is in there, and the ugly stretch of that is the interesting stretch — the wrong guesses, the layer that turned out to be nothing, the four weeks on a floor that held. all of it is visible while it happens, so people watch you be wrong on the way to being right.
moon: the spread has no smaller version of itself. a discreet look into something is not on offer here, because whatever you turn toward is lit at the same width as everything else about you — so the household that would have let you ask quietly gets a public examination instead, and knows it is one. the audience assembles without being called.
pull: nobody consented to the size of it. you go looking, the looking is broadcast, and what you find comes up in the open, in view of the people who were living on it.
tension: the word that follows you is showman, and under it a nastier one — that the digging is done for the room. it sticks because from any seat the audience and the finding arrive together, and nothing you could do would separate them. the ones you were right about remember being watched long after they have stopped disputing that you were right.
cost: what nobody else will do in public, you do in public: name the thing a family or a firm is actually standing on, out loud, where it cannot afterwards be denied that it was said. the private version of that service does not exist anywhere in your life. every person you have been right about was corrected before an audience that will not forget either of you.

lead: nothing you have got to the bottom of has survived the finding by a season. what you are left holding is a list of arrangements that were working until you were curious about them.
sun: other people's findings get absorbed. a fact comes out about how the firm was really set up, everyone adjusts, and the thing carries on in a slightly worse mood. yours are not survivable, because you do not stop at the fact that can be absorbed — you keep going until you reach whatever the arrangement was actually resting on, and by then the resting has been interrupted.
moon: and what follows is never a decline. the weather turns on it — the firm, the friendship, the account of your family that everybody had agreed to keep — and it is over inside a season, entirely, with no residue for someone to work with later. nobody gets the slow bad year in which a case might have been made. one spring it is there, and then it has ended.
pull: the true reason each of them ended is available to you. so is the reason each of them ended, which is that you went looking for the true one.
tension: the invitations thin, and nobody can give a reason for it, since you have not been unkind and have not repeated anything. what does it is the pattern: everyone has now watched an arrangement they liked go under and not come up again, and the story they assemble is that you ruin things. the sequence is real. the intent they attach to it never occurred, and nothing you say detaches it.
cost: a thing that is dying of something nobody can name gets diagnosed by you, correctly, and quickly enough that the diagnosis is the last event in its life. so you have never learned what a marriage or a firm does with the truth about itself, because none of yours has been alive the following season to try.
